correctness.rationale: Selected nonadjacent pairs lie in the same shore and have a distinct two-edge geodesic through every outside vertex. The exact two-clear-geodesic condition gives the three-piece combinatorial Alexander dual Y = union Ai with Ai=sk_{n-3}Delta^{n-1} * discrete(2n). The Ai are high connected sphere-wedges; pair intersections are K_{n,n} and n isolated vertices. When U=A1 union A2, H1 U=Z^n, H2 U=Z^{(n-1)^2}, and U cap A3=K_{2n,n}. The key H1(U cap A3)->H1(U) map has image primitive augmentation ker(Z^n -> Z); four-cycles across the two other shores realize differences [x]-[y], and all cycles reduce to four-cycles. Thus its coker is Z, kernel Z^{2(n-1)^2}; integer Mayer-Vietoris gives free H1,H2,H_{n-2} in dual with ranks 1,3(n-1)^2,3(n-1)(2n-1). Alexander duality on 3n vertices gives claimed degrees and torsion-free groups. Independent finite direct dual enumeration and GF(2) homology for n5,6 matched 750/2076 faces and ranks, not a substitute for integral Mayer-Vietoris.

originality.rationale: Cicerone et al develop fault-tolerant mutual visibility and extremal graph questions but not all-degree integral homology of balanced tripartite complexes. The later published arbitrary-multipartite homology theorem expressly assumes >=4 parts size>=5 and acknowledges balanced THREE-part as earlier distinct work; its formula would have coefficients not justified at t=3 from stated hypotheses. The other published bipartite result requires TWO shores. This tripartite primitive augmentation calculation is thus independently relevant best-of-knowledge.

value.rationale: An exact torsion-free integral homology classification in three noncoincident degrees for a canonical graph family is a natural, non-textbook topological invariant. The primitive lattice image is a nontrivial integral issue invisible to mod-two ranks and establishes the structurally special three-shore threshold between bipartite and four-or-more parts.

final_claim: For balanced K_{n,n,n}, n>=5, one-fault (two internally disjoint clear shortest paths) mutual-visibility complex has exactly three nonzero reduced integral homology groups: Z^{3(n-1)(2n-1)} in degree 2n-1, Z^{3(n-1)^2} in degree 3n-5, and Z in degree 3n-4.
